details: Pfizer never prints Velsipity (etrasimod) revenue. Its fullest product table, the product revenue workbook on investors.pfizer.com (sheets Q1 2026, Q2 2026, YTD Q2 2026), has no Velsipity row and closes Specialty Care with 'All other Specialty Care'; the April 2026 'Recasted 2025 and 2024 Product Revenue Tables' PDF likewise has no Velsipity row. EDGAR full-text search for 'Velsipity' in Pfizer filings returned 19 documents (earnings-release exhibits Q3 2023-Q2 2026, 10-Qs, 10-Ks, ARS); they name it as an approval, a pipeline row, a patent-expiry row, a $1.4 billion IPR&D impairment (Q4 2023), a member of 'Inflammation & immunology' and of 'acquired products' within the 'Launched and Acquired Products' total; none prints a Velsipity revenue figure. No isolated figure exists in any document read. Arena Pharmaceuticals, the prior owner, had no product sales because etrasimod was first approved in October 2023. Everest Medicines (Greater China/Korea licensee) launched in mainland China in March 2026 and has not printed Velsipity sales in the results materials found.

details: Novo Nordisk never prints Esperoct (turoctocog alfa pegol) sales as a table row or a sentence figure. Its most detailed product table, the sales-by-therapy note of the Annual Report 2025 (20-F exhibit nvo-20251231_d2.htm), splits Rare blood disorders only into 'of which Haemophilia A' (a class line that by inference holds NovoEight and Esperoct, possibly more; the report does not say) and 'of which NovoSeven'. EDGAR full-text search for 'Esperoct' in Novo's filings returned 35 documents (all quarterly company announcements caq{q}{yyyy}.htm 2019Q1-2026Q2, the 2019 approval 6-Ks, the 2019 annual report and the FY2020 20-F); every mention is a product list, a footnote ('Comprises NovoSeven, NovoEight, Esperoct, Refixia, NovoThirteen and Alhemo'), a launch-country count (e.g. 'launched in nine countries', FY2019; '10 countries', Q1 2020), a patent table or a growth-driver mention; none carries an Esperoct sales figure. No isolated figure exists in any document read. The 2019 annual report says Novo capitalised two milestone payments to an unnamed business partner on Esperoct's EU and FDA approvals; no partner, royalty holder or earlier owner that publishes Esperoct sales was found.

source_quote: Other HIV (2) | U.S. | 23 | 50 | 59 | 101 ... (2) Includes Atripla, Complera/Eviplera, Emtriva, Stribild, Sunlenca, Truvada and Tybost.
details: Gilead never prints Sunlenca (lenacapavir for treatment of multidrug-resistant HIV-1) on a revenue line of its own. In every quarterly release and Supplementary Information PDF from Q4 2022 (first quarter after the 22 Dec 2022 approval) to Q2 2026 Sunlenca is named only in the footnote to 'Other HIV' (Q4 2022 to Q4 2023: 'Includes Atripla, Emtriva, Sunlenca and Tybost.'; from Q1 2024 the footnote also lists Complera/Eviplera, Stribild and Truvada; Q2 and Q3 2025 also Yeztugo; the Q2 2026 footnote no longer lists Yeztugo). The 10-K and 10-Q revenue notes (FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 10-K; Q2 2026 10-Q) carry the same 'Other HIV' line and footnote. Isolated figure: exactly one Gilead-published Sunlenca sales amount exists, in the Q1 2023 Prepared Remarks PDF (https://s29.q4cdn.com/585078350/files/doc_financials/2023/q1/GILD-Q123-Prepared-Remarks-27-April-2023.pdf: 'Turning to Sunlenca, first quarter sales of $4 million were very much in-line with our expectations.') and the matching Summary of Prepared Remarks ('Sunlenca sales of $4M, in line with expectations.'). No other quarter's prepared remarks (Q4 2022, Q2 2023 to Q2 2026, 14 further quarters) states a Sunlenca amount, so a single quarter is all that exists and is not a series. No annual figure exists either. Inferred, not measured: Sunlenca revenue sits inside 'Other HIV'.
